3. Calcium, magnesium, and sodium concentrations from waters of the Rosebud-McKay coal showed no apparent areal pattern. Sodium was the predominant cation found in water from the Robinson and Sub-Robinson zones. Minor levels of potassium (usually less than 10 mg/1) were detected in all ground water samples.
4. Three alluvium wells were sampled; two on Sarpy and one on East Fork Sarpy Creeks. The water quality was similar in all wells, with magnesium and sodium concentrations slightly higher than calcium. Dissolved solids ranged from 1,315 mg/l to 1,691 mg/l and sulfate concentrations ranged from 617 mg/l to 788 mg/l.

Strontium was the only trace element found in relatively high concentrations; concentrations ranged from 0.8 mg/l to 11.8 mg/l, with a 3.5 mg/l average for all aquifers sampled. Boron concentrations ranged from 0.04 mg/l to 0.85 mg/l, with an average of 0.35 mg/l for all samples.
Dames and Moore (1975, p. 10 and 20) provide comments on the monitoring wells sampled in October and November 1975. With regard to Tract III, there had been a general increase in the concentration of most major constituents in wells 1A(ROB), 1B(SR), and 2A(RMC) (located in the Robinson Coal, Sub-Robinson Zone, and Rosebud-McKay Coal, respectively), since the summer of 1975.
